Layer 01 of 07 · OSB / plank

The deck: bare wood, photographed

Everything comes off down to the boards. We photograph every sheet, circle the soft ones and ask before we replace them, at $70–$110 per 4x8 sheet Sample pricing.

“They texted me photos of the decking after tear-off, two soft spots circled by the chimney, and asked before replacing them. First time a roofer ever showed me the wood under my shingles.”

Kevin D., Derby · Sample review

Layers 02 + 03 · Edge & membrane

Drip edge, then ice shield at every eave

Metal along the eave sends water into the gutter, not behind the fascia. Peel-and-stick membrane goes over it at eaves, valleys and pipes, where ice dams and wind-driven rain get in. Both are new on every job.

Drag the line: edge metal first, membrane on top.

03 · Ice shield
02 · Drip edge

Layer 04 of 07 · Synthetic underlayment

Synthetic felt that lies flat when it gets wet

It is tougher than the old paper felt, it does not wrinkle under a summer storm, and it gives the crew sure footing on a steep pitch.

“Our 1958 ranch had two roofs stacked on each other. They stripped both, found the old plank boards, and sheathed over them. It ran a day longer than planned and they called before every change. Fair people.”

Walt H., Valley Center · Full roof replacement · Sample review

Layer 05 of 07 · Starter strip

The first course nobody sees

An adhesive starter row seals the eave edge so the first shingles cannot lift in a Kansas gust. Skip it and that is where the leak starts.

Where
Eaves and rakes
Why
Wind uplift
Checked
Photo before shingles

Layer 06 of 07 · Architectural shingles

Six nails a shingle. Class 4 if hail keeps finding you.

Sealed tabs, six-nail pattern, courses snapped to a chalk line. Impact-rated Class 4 shingles are an option; ask your insurer whether they lower the premium.

Full replacement $9,500–$17,500 · typical 1,800-2,400 sq ft ranch Sample pricing

Layer 07 of 07 · Ridge cap & vent

Ridge vent out, soffit air in

Hot attic air leaves through the ridge; cool air comes in at the soffits. Balanced, it stops summer heat from cooking the shingles from underneath. Then the cap goes on and the photo packet is done.

After layer 07

Then the yard. Magnet sweep, twice.

The dumpster leaves before we do. Two passes with the magnet over lawn, beds and driveway, so no nail ends up in a tire or a paw.

“June hail took out half the shingles on our west side. Crew was done in a day and a half, ran the magnet over the yard twice, and the dog found zero nails.”

Rosa M., Andover · Sample review

What we take on

Four calls we get most

  1. 01

    Roof check

    We walk every slope, photograph what is worn and tell you what can wait.

  2. 02

    Leak repair

    We trace water back to where it gets in, not just where it drips onto the ceiling.

  3. 03

    Full roof replacement

    Torn off to bare wood, soft boards replaced, then rebuilt one photographed layer at a time.

  4. 04

    Hail and wind repair

    Bruised shingles, lifted tabs and dented vents found, photographed and replaced to match.

And the specialty work

  • Impact-resistant shinglesClass 4 shingles made to take Kansas hail; ask your insurer whether they lower your premium.
  • Flashing and chimney workNew step flashing, counterflashing and chimney crickets, the places most leaks begin.
  • Metal roofingStanding-seam panels for porches, shops and whole houses, with hidden clips and sealed seams.
  • Skylight install and resealNew or resealed skylights with fresh flashing kits, so light comes in and rain stays out.
  • Storm tarpingA tarp battened over the damage so the next rain stays outside while repairs are planned.
  • Attic and ridge ventingRidge vents and soffit intake balanced so summer attic heat stops cooking shingles from below.
